doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Olympic athletes analogy on defection from socialist and capitalist countries
summary: He argues that people flee Cuba and the Soviet bloc, not the reverse, and urges listeners to read about Eastern Europe.

blocks.x: countries. It has always been the other way around. Athletes from the former Soviet Union or the former Eastern European countries asking for political asylum. So in places like the United States or Belgium or France and any capitalist country where the game has been celebrated. So I think that tells you something, that if people defect from a system that many people of the world think it is perfect, why don’t people from those countries defect and the people from the terrible countries like the United States or the poorest countries in Africa or South America, they didn’t ask for political asylum in the former Soviet Union. So that’s my point. When I see the rafts going from the Gulf Coast of Florida to Cuba and I see Americans and people going to Cuba asking for political asylum then I’m going to say uh oh, that is something now very wrong with the system. But up to now it’s the other way around. People in Cuba risk their life to go across the Caribbean and come to the United States and ask for political asylum. So that’s one of the reasons why because of the promises that the Cuban government made, in this case Fidel Castro who was the government. All the promises that he made that he didn’t fulfill and the repressive system that he installed in Cuba and so forth and so on. So people who want to know more about this, I think they just should get educated and read about the former Soviet Union, former European countries — Eastern European countries — and they’re going to find a lot of answers.
